messages.subject: make data centroid and apply function on imageData()[]

Hello,

I am trying to use the Cardinal package to read MSI data and face a few problem so I would like to know if I am doing it right.
I used previously the readmzxml package to read MS data and output is quite different.

Here is my code:


library(maggritr)
library(Cardinal)

## Set some options
mass.accuracy = 0.025
resolution_redim = 3
Int_threshold = 2000
initial_dim = 30

## Read the data file: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2Fs00216-014-8357-8
data = Cardinal::readImzML("HR2MSI mouse urinary bladder S096",
                           mass.accuracy = mass.accuracy,units.accuracy = "mz")

## extract the dense matrix
data2 = imageData(data)[features(data),seq(from=1,to=260,by=resolution_redim),seq(from=1,to=134,by=resolution_redim)]
# print(dim(data2))
# print(sum(apply(data2,1,max)>Int_threshold))

## apply the threshold
data2 = data2[which(apply(data2,1,max)>Int_threshold),,]

# the rest is my analysis, I put it so you understand what I am doing
## flatten the array (DLC package on github: https://github.com/DimitriF/DLC), this lead to a matrix with one row per masses and one column per pixel
decon  = DLC::deconstruct(truc,margin=1,transform=T)

## normalization and first dimension reduction
model = decon %>%
  prospectr::standardNormalVariate() %>%
  ChemometricsWithR::PCA()
data3 = model$scores[,1:initial_dim]

## second dimension reduction with tsne
set.seed(1)
model2 = Rtsne(mat,dims = 2,perplexity = 5,max_iter = 1000,verbose = F,pca = F)

## plot the tsne map, similar images clusterize together
plot(model2$Y,pch=".")


And my questions:

- The data is in profile format and not centroid as I am used to, is there a way to make the peak peaking before the bining ?
- Is there a "apply like" function to apply the intensity threshold filtering before extracting the dense array ? I need to remove low intensity masses later anyway.
- For the analysis, do you have something similar ?

The documentation was quite extensive and there are lots of functions in this package so I apologize if the answer was already present.

Regards
Dimitri

messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Re: make data centroid and apply function on imageData()[]
parts:
Hi Dimitri,

1. Yes, the walkthrough vignette as well as the workflow vignettes from the CardinalWorkflows have examples of peak picking and binning.

http://bioconductor.org/packages/release/data/experiment/vignettes/CardinalWorkflows/inst/doc/Workflows-clustering.pdf
http://bioconductor.org/packages/release/data/experiment/vignettes/CardinalWorkflows/inst/doc/Workflows-classification.pdf

2. There are pixelApply() and featureApply() functions, yes. These will work on the pixels or mass features, respectively.

3. There is a Cardinal::PCA() function for performing PCA; t-SNE is not currently implemented natively.

It looks like you are going through extra trouble to change the data from datacube into matrix format where rows are features and columns are pixels. This is how the data is internally stored and can be accessed via the iData() accessor . (There is also a spectra() accessor alias for it.)

-Kylie

Hi Kylie,

I just made one session and already managed to do what I wanted thanks to the Cardinal package. The main difference to classic 1D data is that there are much more pixels in an image than time-step in a chromatogram, I will find my way with this new data type (once I read the doc carefully...)

I found the featureApply yesterday, it was slow but what I was looking for (same reason, too much pixels)

For the PCA, I don't think your function do what I did with tsne, I used mz (features) as rows and pixels as column where you do the opposite, so the point in the 2D map are ions, not pixels. We use the approach in my lab for structure elucidation, it is some kind of deisotoping.

The extra trouble is standard in my workflow, my main data source are images of HPTLC which comes in 3d array (data cube), I am use to deconstruct and reconstruct the data cube. The iData() function may help me go faster and it looks indeed close to the output of the readmzXMLdata function.

Dimitri
